title: Context and memory in an agent

items.stem: On Monday a student chats with your makerspace assistant and says she prefers morning slots. On Wednesday she starts a new chat. The assistant does not know her preference. What explains this?

options.text: The model forgets old chats because its context window was full
The model stores chats only for a short time before deleting them
Nothing was saved by the program and loaded into the new chat
The model needs a longer system prompt to remember its users

items.stem: Your first model call has 1,050 input tokens. The model replies with a 60-token tool request. The tool returns 2,000 tokens, and the program calls the model a second time, which writes the final answer. Counting both calls, how many input tokens were sent in total?
Your manuals total 400 pages and your model's context window could hold all of them. Which design is best for answering a question about one machine's focus procedure?

options.text: Put all manuals in the system prompt so every call has them
Give the model a search tool that returns the best few chunks
Fine-tune the model on the manuals so that it remembers them
Save each manual page as a note and load every note each time

items.stem: In one sentence: why does each extra step in an agent loop cost more input tokens than the step before it, even when each tool result is small?
Which one of these is the best candidate to save as a note that the assistant loads in future sessions?

options.text: The student completed laser cutter safety training on a given date
The laser cutter is free next Tuesday afternoon, as just checked
The full text of the laser cutter's maintenance chapter, as retrieved
The model's reasoning for choosing the calendar tool in this chat
